segments.text: When we experience strong emotions, we often use very broad brushstrokes to describe the emotions.
I'm stressed is the most common one I hear, but there's a world of difference between stress
and disappointment or stress and anxiety. When we move beyond these big umbrella terms
to label our emotions accurately, it enables our body and our psychology to take what can
feel immense and difficult and define some parameters around it. So next time you feel a strong
emotion, remember that words matter, see if you can move beyond the broad brushstroke and ask yourself
what are two other options? What else might I be feeling? When you do this, you enable yourself
to move from being stuck in the difficulty emotion into being able to activate what scientists
call a readiness potential, the ability to move forward with and in spite of the emotion.
